requirement:
Habeas MUST parse Rust, Python, TypeScript, CSS, Markdown, TOML, and YAML
sources with pinned tree-sitter grammars, selected by file extension compared
case-insensitively. A source with any syntax error MUST fail to parse, reporting
the line of its first error. Every
other text file MUST use a plain-text profile in which each line that is not
blank is an anonymous outline node of kind `line`. Each supported language MUST
have an outline profile that maps grammar node kinds to short outline kind names
and, for each mapped kind, states whether a node is named, and by which fields
or children, or anonymous. Only mapped kinds MUST appear in the outline; other
nodes MUST be transparent, so their outline descendants appear under the
nearest outline ancestor. A profile MAY attach grammar siblings to an outline
node, such as Rust attributes and doc comments preceding an item, so the outline
tree need not match the grammar tree exactly; attached siblings are part of that
node for its line range and hash. Every file's outline MUST have a root node
for the whole file, independent of language. Source in no other outline node,
such as top-level statements no profile maps, MUST belong to the root node;
profiles MUST NOT invent fallback kinds for it. Comments MUST NOT be outline nodes. Profiles MUST be
documented. Upgrading a grammar or profile MAY change outlines and MUST be
treated as a deliberate change.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation in `requirements.references.outlines`.

- **Languages and extension selection.**
  - `profiles_are_selected_by_extension_case_insensitively` checks uppercase and mixed-case extensions. These map to rust, python, tsx, markdown and toml. It also checks that `notes` and `notes.rs.txt` fall back to plain text.
  - `every_profile_mapping_is_documented` iterates every profile's extensions.
  - The per-language profile tests parse Rust, Python, TypeScript and TSX, CSS, Markdown, TOML and YAML.
- **Pinned grammars.** `grammar_dependencies_are_pinned_to_exact_versions` asserts that every `tree-sitter-*` dependency in Cargo.toml uses an exact `=x.y.z` pin.
- **Syntax errors.** `reports_parse_failures_with_lines` covers Rust, Python and TOML. The Rust case asserts that the error line is 2. The TOML case has several errors and asserts that the first one (line 3) is reported, with the `line 3: ` message prefix. That is the "first error" obligation. I read `check_errors`, which handles both error nodes and missing nodes in one generic path. So the tests don't need a case per language or error kind.
- **Plain text.** `plain_text_lines_are_interchangeable_anonymous_nodes` asserts that blank lines are skipped and that each non-blank line is a `line@…` node. `outline_lists_nested_nodes_without_text_or_inputs` asserts that every plain-text entry has kind `line` and a null name.
- **Profile kind mapping.** The Rust, Python, TypeScript, CSS, Markdown, TOML and YAML tests assert the mapped kinds, names and anonymity (`section@`, `item@`, `use@`, `macro@`). `profile_rules_map_only_matching_contexts_and_keep_other_nodes_transparent` shows that unmapped kinds are not emitted. In that test, descendants of an unmapped node are reparented to the nearest mapped ancestor, here the root. `item_macros_are_anonymous_nodes_and_expression_macros_are_not` covers the same point from the other side.
- **Attached siblings.** `hashes_skip_whitespace_and_plain_comments_but_not_doc_comments` asserts that a node's line range spans its doc comment and attribute (1 to 4). It also asserts that these siblings change the node's hash. `identity_hashes_include_own_attached_siblings_but_not_descendants` covers the identity hash.
- **Root node.**
  - `outline.resolve("")` returns 0 in `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry`.
  - `file_level_inner_doc_comments_and_unmapped_code_belong_to_the_root` and `python_profile_outlines_defs_classes_and_statements` check that unmapped top-level code, file-level doc comments and front matter belong to the root.
  - `line_queries_find_innermost_nodes` maps a blank line to the root.
- **No fallback kinds.** `no_profile_invents_fallback_kinds` runs every language with unmapped top-level statements. It asserts that no `stmt`, `block`, `node` or `item` fallback kinds appear and that only the root exists where nothing is mapped.
- **Comments are not nodes.** The Rust, Python, CSS, TOML, YAML and Markdown tests contain comments. Their exact selector and summary assertions would fail if a comment became a node.
- **Documentation.** `every_profile_mapping_is_documented` checks every profile's extensions and every kind rule against the "Outline profiles" table in `md/reference.md`. It also checks the plain-text row.
- **Grammar upgrades.** This is a process obligation with a MAY. It is not testable and imposes nothing.

I found no requirement-violating behavior that these assertions would accept.
